tones: Deep dive — explain the concept from first principles, build it up piece by piece, no hand-waving
TIL / learning in public — something I finally understood today, shared honestly as a discovery
Myth-busting — correct one common misconception about how AI actually works, with the real version
Analogy-driven — one clean analogy that makes a hard concept genuinely click
Under the hood — what literally happens inside the model, step by step, during a forward pass
Engineering gotcha — a subtle failure mode and the mental model that explains and fixes it

formats: learning-in-public moment — 'I finally understand X. here is what it actually is.' 2-3 lines, honest, first-person discovery.
mechanism in plain language — explain how one concept works. specific, accurate, no jargon soup. 2-4 short lines.
myth vs reality — 'everyone thinks X. what actually happens: Y.' one clear, specific contrast.
one surprising fact — a single thing that is technically true and non-obvious. just the fact and what it means.
step-by-step breakdown — how something works in 3-4 concrete steps. each step is one short line.
concept comparison — two things that seem similar but work differently. nail the key difference in 2-3 lines.

pattern_interrupts: Wrong Assumption Snap — state the common belief as flat fact, then deny it in the very next clause. e.g. 'everyone thinks fine-tuning teaches new facts. it doesn't.'
Mid-Thought Drop — open like you're already mid-explanation, no throat-clearing. e.g. 'so it turns out the cache isn't optional — it's the entire reason chat feels instant.'
Cold Number Open — lead with one specific, unexpected number before any context. e.g. '128k tokens of context and it still forgets line 40.'
Flat Confession — one short, unhedged admission of being wrong, no self-deprecating padding. e.g. 'I didn't get attention for six months. then this clicked.'
Reversal Statement — say the exact opposite of what the reader expects the sentence to end with. e.g. 'temperature has nothing to do with creativity.'
Direct Address — speak straight at the person mid-problem, no wind-up. e.g. 'if your RAG keeps returning garbage, it's probably not the model.'
psychological_triggers: Competence Check — implies the reader might be doing it wrong right now, triggering an instant self-audit. Must stay factual, never manipulative-empty.
Insider Detail — surfaces something the paper or docs gloss over. 'the paper doesn't say this part out loud, but...'
Myth vs Mechanism (cognitive dissonance) — state the common belief, then contradict it with the real mechanism, forcing a mental-model update.
Shared Struggle — names a specific, relatable debugging pain so readers feel 'seen' and want to reply with their own version. 'if you've ever debugged this at 2am, you know.'
Vulnerability-as-Authority — admit confusion before delivering the insight; builds trust because it isn't lecturing.
Unresolved Tension — pose two things that seem contradictory and let the post reconcile them; the brain can't let an open contradiction sit.
curiosity_gaps: The Open Loop — state the surprising result first, defer the reason to the very next sentence. 'the bug wasn't in my code. it was in how I was counting tokens.'
The Withheld Mechanism — hint that one specific detail explains everything, without naming it yet. 'there's one line in the attention formula that explains this entire failure mode.'
Setup → Payoff Gap — describe the confusing symptom first, resolve it with the mechanism only in the second half of the post.
The Partial Reveal — give most of the picture, hold the exact number or detail back for the next sentence.
The 'One Thing' Frame — 'there's exactly one design choice that makes this possible' — narrows attention to a single answer worth reading for.
Hard rule for every gap: it MUST resolve with a real technical answer inside the same post. No gap is allowed to go unclosed — this is structuring a real insight for pull, not clickbait.
power_phrases: here's the part nobody explains clearly
I got this wrong for a while
the model isn't doing what you think it's doing
it was never doing X. it was doing Y.
the reason is dumber than you'd expect
hook_structures: Myth → Mechanism: state the widespread wrong belief, then the real mechanism that corrects it. (the natural engine for Style 1 — Problem → Solution)
Scenario → Breakdown: open on a concrete failure a builder hits, then explain the mechanism behind it. (the natural engine for Style 2 — Scenario → Risk → Solution)
Confession → Discovery: admit not understanding something, then narrate the exact detail that made it click.
Number → Explanation: open on one specific, surprising number or stat, then unpack why it's true.
Direct Correction: 'X doesn't do Y. it does Z.' — snaps a wrong mental model straight in one line.
Question Nobody Asks: pose a question most people never think to ask about a familiar tool, then answer it technically.
